condition: pediatric accidental corrosive alkaline ingestion in a 2-year-old toddler who swallowed lye liquid drain cleaner from a low kitchen cabinet
level_rationale: Ingesting a mouthful of corrosive alkaline lye liquid drain cleaner 10 minutes ago in a 2-year-old toddler carries immediate risk of progressive pharyngeal airway edema and transmural esophageal liquefactive necrosis requiring immediate emergency department airway evaluation and endoscopic assessment, whereas swallowing a mouthful of food-grade canola cooking oil from a low kitchen cabinet 10 minutes ago is non-toxic and requires home observation only.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain parent-carer lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 syntactic-frame by clinical/everyday lexical crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + causal belief-addition clause (-att) + benign household cooking-oil ingestion self-care control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (2-year-old son, accessing a low kitchen cabinet 10 minutes ago, and swallowing a mouthful of corrosive alkaline lye drain cleaner) with a 1-word span difference (17 vs 18 words). Placing the ingested household substance in f3 prevents stranding swallowed caustic cleaner or chemical burns when f3 shifts under Rule A and Rule D to swallowing a mouthful of food-grade canola cooking oil from the same low kitchen cabinet (level 4 ER to level 1 home self-care) with zero stated negatives.
